title: The imperative
description: Affirmative and negative commands for tu, noi, voi and formal Lei/Loro; irregular short forms; position of pronouns.
objectives: Form the imperative of regular and irregular verbs.
Form the negative tu imperative with non + infinitive.
Use the formal Lei imperative (from the congiuntivo presente).
Place object and reflexive pronouns correctly, including the doubled consonant after va', fa', da', di', sta'.

blocks.title: tu: -a for -are verbs, -i for the others
blocks.text: For tu, -are verbs use the lui/lei present form (*parla!*); -ere and -ire verbs use the tu present form (*prendi! dormi! finisci!*). noi and voi are identical to the present (*parliamo! parlate!*).

blocks.title: Formal Lei and Loro
blocks.text: The formal forms are borrowed from the congiuntivo presente: *(Lei) parli! prenda! venga!* Formal plural *Loro* (*parlino!*) is now limited to very formal service language; ordinarily *voi* is used for several people.

blocks.title: No imperative
blocks.text: *potere* and *dovere* have no imperative. The imperative of *volere* (*vogli, vogliate*) is rare and literary.

blocks.title: tu: non + infinitive
blocks.text: *Non parlare! Non prendere! Non andare!* For all other persons, put non before the affirmative form: *Non parliamo! Non parlate! Non parli!* (Lei).

blocks.title: Attached to tu, noi, voi
blocks.text: Object and reflexive pronouns follow and attach to the tu, noi and voi forms: *guardalo! alzati! alziamoci! sedetevi! dimmelo!* With Lei and Loro they precede: *lo guardi! si alzi!*

blocks.title: Doubling after the short forms
blocks.text: After *va', da', fa', di', sta'* the consonant of the pronoun doubles: *dammi* (give me), *fallo* (do it), *dimmi* (tell me), *vattene* (go away), *stammi bene*. Exception: *gli* does not double (*dagli*).

blocks.title: Negative tu: two positions
blocks.text: With the negative tu imperative the pronoun may attach to the infinitive or precede it: *Non alzarti! = Non ti alzare!* *Non dirlo! = Non lo dire!* Both are standard.

examples.it: Non toccare il forno: è caldo!
examples.en: Don't touch the oven: it's hot!

examples.note: Formal Lei: pronoun before the verb.

exercises.explanation: -are → -a; -ere/-ire → -i (with -isc- where the present has it); irregular sii, abbi, di'.
The negative tu imperative is non + infinitive. Non vada! is the formal Lei form.
Formal Lei uses the congiuntivo presente: venga.

mistakes.message: vieni is the informal tu form. Formal Lei: venga.

exercises.explanation: After fa' the l of lo doubles: fallo.

mistakes.message: After the short form fa' the consonant doubles: fallo.

exercises.explanation: voi imperative + attached reflexive pronoun vi: sedetevi.
Both positions of the pronoun are standard with the negative tu imperative.
Pronoun attached to tu/noi/voi; before the verb with Lei.

summary: tu: -a (-are), -i (-ere/-ire); noi and voi = present; Lei/Loro = congiuntivo presente.
Irregular: va'/vai, da'/dai, fa'/fai, sta'/stai, di', sii, abbi, sappi.
Negative tu: non + infinitive. Other persons: non + affirmative form.
Pronouns attach to tu/noi/voi (dimmi, alziamoci), precede Lei/Loro (si alzi); consonants double after va', da', fa', di', sta'.
